recommendation_summary: The reply recommends a single hosted dead man's switch (e.g. healthchecks.io), pinged by nightly_sync.py at start and on successful completion with a ~90-minute grace period, so the user is alerted when the job fails or doesn't run.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You asked to know immediately when nightly-sync fails, without reading logs; the trigger is last week's four-night silent outage (expired token, crashed before the email step, so no email, no alert, nobody noticed).
labels.Deleted: a central Synology/Docker log-aggregation stack (ELK/Grafana/Loki style). It doesn't fix the actual problem, you already said you won't read logs, and there's nothing else on edna today that needs cross-job log search.
labels.Bottleneck: there's no alert on a missing expected event. The job can die before it ever reaches the email step, so a crash and a quiet success day look identical to you.
labels.Checked myself: this is from what you've told me, cron on edna at 03:00, success sends an email, it crashed at the token step four nights running with zero other alerting in place.

note: The reply recommends one heartbeat check, rejects both the Synology/Docker log stack and a self-hosted heartbeat, and its Checked myself line rests only on facts the user gave.
